one_line: Three key voices of the 12th‑century Kannada vachana tradition and its early memory in Karnataka.

appearance.age_look: Akka Mahadevi: early 20s, slender; Basavanna: late 30s–40s, sturdy; Harihara: early 30s, medium build.
appearance.face: Akka: heart-shaped face, wheatish complexion, large thoughtful eyes, calm inward gaze; Basavanna: broad oval face, warm medium-brown complexion, strong brows, steady compassionate eyes, gentle serious expression; Harihara: slightly long face, fairer wheatish tone, sharp observant eyes, faint scholarly smile.
appearance.hair: Akka: long black hair in a single thick braid down her back, braid wrapped with a plain white cloth near the end, small central parting, simple copper maang-tikka on forehead; Basavanna: neatly combed black hair tied in a low knot at the back, short trimmed moustache, ash-mark (vibhuti) on forehead beneath a small tied white cloth headband; Harihara: shoulder-length wavy black hair tucked behind ears, no facial hair, small tilaka on forehead, simple dark-brown cloth headscarf loosely tied back leaving top of head visible.
appearance.costume: Akka Mahadevi wears a modest, full-length off-white cotton sari in early medieval Karnataka drape, pleats at front and the pallu drawn over both shoulders and across the chest, with a faint handwoven border in pale leaf-green; under it a short-sleeved off-white cotton blouse fully covering her torso; she has a simple tulasi-bead necklace, small copper earrings, and bare forearms with no bangles. Basavanna wears a knee-length pale-sandalwood-coloured cotton tunic (angarakha style) with long sleeves and a wrapped front tied at the side, over a full-length dark indigo cotton dhoti with a thin white border, pleats in front and draped to the ankles; over the tunic he has a plain brick-red cotton shawl folded and draped over the left shoulder and across his chest; he also wears a rudraksha and lingam pendant necklace, simple wooden beads around his wrists, and leather sandals. Harihara wears a full-length deep-emerald-green cotton uttariya shawl wrapped over both shoulders and crossing the chest, over a light-cream knee-length kurta with long narrow sleeves, and a saffron-bordered white dhoti tied at the waist and reaching the ankles; he has a thin waist cord visible at the kurta hem, a simple single-strand bead necklace, and unadorned feet. All three are fully and modestly clothed in era-appropriate, draped garments.
appearance.signature: A single shared palm-leaf manuscript bundle, wrapped in deep maroon cloth and tied with a thin cotton cord, held slightly forward by Basavanna with Akka Mahadevi and Harihara close beside him, symbolising their vachanas and early biographical memory.

ref_desc: Akka Mahadevi, Basavanna and Harihara stand together with Akka in off-white sari and braid, Basavanna in pale tunic, indigo dhoti and red shawl, Harihara in cream kurta and green shawl, all holding a maroon-wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle.
sheet_prompt: Draw three full-body anime-style figures from 12th-century Karnataka standing side by side: Akka Mahadevi, Basavanna and Harihara. Akka is a slender young woman with a heart-shaped face, wheatish skin and large thoughtful eyes, her long black hair in a single thick braid wrapped near the end with a plain white cloth; she has a small copper maang-tikka and wears a modest off-white cotton sari with a faint pale leaf-green border, pleats in front and the pallu brought over both shoulders and across her chest, over a short-sleeved off-white blouse that fully covers her torso, with a simple tulasi-bead necklace and small copper earrings. Basavanna is sturdier, late 30s–40s, with a broad oval face, medium-brown complexion, strong brows and a calm serious expression; his black hair is tied in a low knot, he has a short trimmed moustache and an ash-mark on his forehead under a narrow white cloth headband; he wears a pale sandalwood-coloured long-sleeved cotton tunic wrapped and tied at the side, over a full-length dark indigo cotton dhoti with a thin white border, pleated in front and reaching his ankles, and a plain brick-red cotton shawl folded over his left shoulder and across his chest, with a rudraksha and lingam pendant necklace, bead wristbands and simple leather sandals. Harihara is early 30s, medium build, with a slightly long face, fairer wheatish tone, sharp observant eyes and a faint scholarly smile; his shoulder-length wavy black hair is tucked behind his ears, with a small tilaka on his forehead and a dark-brown cloth headscarf tied loosely back; he wears a light-cream knee-length kurta with narrow long sleeves under a deep emerald-green cotton uttariya shawl wrapped over both shoulders and across the chest, above a saffron-bordered white dhoti tied at the waist and reaching the ankles, with a thin waist cord and bare feet. Basavanna holds forward one shared deep maroon cloth-wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a cotton cord, with Akka and Harihara standing close beside him, all depicted in a consistent earthy palette of off-white, dark indigo, brick red, emerald green and maroon, in a clean model-sheet view that clearly shows their faces, hairstyles, garments and the manuscript bundle from head to toe.
